record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.original_question: Does there exist a division algebra that is finitely generated, algebraic, and infinite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Do there exist infinite dimensional finitely generated algebraic division algebras?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field. A $K$-algebra $D$ is called a division algebra if $D$ is an associative (not necessarily commutative) $K$-algebra with $1$ in which every nonzero element has a two-sided multiplicative inverse. We say $D$ is finitely generated (as a $K$-algebra) if there exist finitely many elements $d_1,\dots,d_n \in D$ such that $D$ is generated by $d_1,\dots,d_n$ together with $1$ under the operations of addition, scalar multiplication by $K$, and multiplication. We say $D$ is algebraic over $K$ if every element of $D$ is a root of some nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $K$. Finally, $D$ is infinite-dimensional if $\dim_K D = \infty$.

Does there exist a field $K$ and a $K$-algebra $D$ such that $D$ is simultaneously a division algebra, finitely generated as a $K$-algebra, algebraic over $K$, and infinite-dimensional over $K$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Kurosh problem for division rings, posed by A. G. Kurosh in 1941. While Golod–Shafarevich (1964) gave finitely generated infinite-dimensional algebraic (nil) algebras, the division-algebra case remains open: a finitely generated algebraic division ring is not known to be centrally finite. Recent work (e.g., the "Quantitative Kurosh Problem" in Forum of Mathematics Sigma and works on algebraicity of bounded degree in division rings, 2022) explicitly refers to it as still open.

status_evidence.title: Kurosh problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Kurosh Problem for division rings asks whether a finitely generated algebraic division ring is centrally finite. This longstanding problem posed in 1941 remains without answer.
status_evidence.claim: The division-algebra version of the Kurosh problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Quantitative Kurosh Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative version of the still-unresolved Kurosh problem for division rings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to treat the division-ring Kurosh problem as open.

status_evidence.title: On the algebraicity of bounded degree in division rings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies algebraic division rings in connection with the Kurosh problem.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on this open problem as of 2022.
